When the NPC asks questions or names conditions, the client harness composes the next natural player turn from the actual NPC reply, answers relevant identity, authority, household, compensation, status, route, provision, and security concerns, accepts NPC-authored conditions without changing permanent affiliation, and asks for unmistakable final consent. Negotiation, conditional interest, or a clarification request is not consent. A guest may refuse a player-requested departure and remain Active; departure is queued only after the NPC accepts, while ordinary Reign arrest and imprisonment behavior remains unchanged and outside Party Agency. A live temporary guest's battle and civilian equipment are immutable through Bannerlord's native equipment gate and Reign item actions. Direct action invocation cannot satisfy a case. Structured MCP commands are limited to fixture, time, save/load, battle, provider-fault, and evidence control.

externalContinuity.behavior: Closes only the Codex desktop app. The watchdog captures all unfinished Codex tasks and reopens them in Codex Desktop. Recovery is Desktop-only for both planned MCP restarts and unexpected closures; the watchdog never starts a hidden codex exec resume process. After an unexpected closure, the durable task may require a normal continuation message in Desktop.
externalContinuity.ownershipGate: Codex Desktop is the only recovery writer. Windows or the user may activate a task independently of the watchdog, so a background recovery CLI cannot be made reliably exclusive. Prohibiting every hidden codex exec resume process prevents open-in-another-app locks, competing mutations, and missing-tool-host retry loops.
externalContinuity.precondition: Write a durable task checkpoint and use only when a Codex restart is required.
externalContinuity.fallback: If recovery is incomplete, reopen the durable task and re-observe uncertain external operations before continuing.
